style: Under Hong Myung-bo the side has shifted toward a back-three, built on relentless work rate, quick transitions and counter-attacking. Korea rarely dominates possession against top opponents, instead relying on intensity, pressing and the individual quality of Son and Lee Kang-in to create chances.
recent_form: Comfortable qualifiers from Asia and a settled core under Hong Myung-bo. Solid but not spectacular, with attention on the back-three experiment and Son's fitness as the veteran captain prepares for a fourth World Cup. In Group A with co-host Mexico, South Africa and Czechia.

key_players.name: Son Heung-min
key_players.note: 33-year-old all-time caps record holder at his fourth World Cup; Korea's most potent attacking weapon with pace and finishing.

key_players.name: Kim Min-jae
key_players.note: Bayern Munich centre-back, regarded as the best defender Korea has produced; dominant aerially and key to building out.

key_players.name: Lee Kang-in
key_players.note: PSG midfielder offering elite vision and passing range; the main creative outlet beyond fast breaks.

key_players.name: Hwang Hee-chan
key_players.note: Pacey, direct attacker effective in transition alongside Son.

key_players.name: Hwang In-beom
key_players.note: Tidy two-way midfielder who controls tempo and links defence to attack.

historical_news: Son Heung-min captains Korea at his fourth World Cup, holding the national caps record (144).
Hong Myung-bo shifted the team to a back-three system, sparking debate over defensive stability and attacking balance.
Kim Min-jae anchors the defence as one of the Bundesliga's top centre-backs.
Korea reached the round of 16 at the 2022 World Cup with a dramatic final-group win over Portugal.
Drawn into Group A alongside co-host Mexico, South Africa and Czechia.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Steady confidence built on star quality in Son, Kim and Lee, with uncertainty over Hong's back-three system and the squad's depth against elite sides.
